{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative bias (e.g., -0.25 or below) to counteract overconfidence.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% if recent true outcomes show mean reversion toward lower levels after a spike.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative (0.00–0.33) to avoid underestimating downside risk.",
    "Apply a lag correction: if true outcome is significantly lower than forecast 3–5 days prior, adjust current forecast downward by 3–7%.",
    "Avoid over-optimism after sharp price spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >15% in 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 10–20% for next period.",
    "When sentiment history includes 0.50 or higher, increase forecast volatility to reflect heightened market uncertainty or speculative behavior.",
    "If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by >5% over 5+ days, apply a ‘mean reversion’ bias: shift forecast toward historical 30-day average, not model trend."
  ]
}
